farraa:1-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلطَّارِقِ﴾.
الطارق: the star, because it rises at night; whatever comes to you at night is a طارق. Then He explained it and said: ﴿النَّجْمُ الثَّاقِبُ﴾. الثاقب: the shining one. The Arabs say to the one kindling a fire: أثقب نارك (make your fire blaze). It is also said that الثاقب is the star called Zuḥal (Saturn); and الثاقب is the one that has risen above the stars. The Arabs say of a bird when it reaches the belly of the sky in height: قد ثقّب. All of that has come in the exegesis.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّمَّا عَلَيْهَا﴾.
The general public read it "لمّا", and some read it lightened; al-Kisāʾī used to read it lightened. We do not know the rationale for the doubled form, and we consider it a dialect of Hudhayl, who use (لمّا) for إلا together with the lightened إنْ, and do not go beyond that. As though He said [«قالك» in the source]: there is no soul but that over it [134/b] there is a guardian.
Whoever reads it lightened says: it is only the lām of the response to إنْ, and the (ما) after it is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant), as in His saying: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ ميثاقهم﴾. He says: so there is no doubling in (ما) when it is a ṣila.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَلَيْهَا حَافِظٌ﴾.
The guardian from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, guards it until He hands it over to the decrees [of fate].

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِن مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ﴾.
The people of the Ḥijāz do this more than others: making the passive [participle] active when it is used as an adjective, as in the Arabs' saying: هذا سرٌّ كاتم (a concealing secret, i.e. a concealed secret), همٌّ ناصبٌ (a toiling care, i.e. a wearying care), ليلٌ نائمٌ (a sleeping night) and عيشةٌ راضيةٌ (a pleased life, i.e. a pleasing life). What helped this is that it agrees with the verse-endings that it accompanies.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِن بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ﴾.
He means: from the backbone and the breastbones. It is permissible to say of two things: ليخرجنّ من بين هذين خير كثير (much good will come forth from between these two), and من هذين (from these two). الصلب: the man's backbone; الترائب: what surrounds the upper chest of the woman, where the necklaces lie.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ﴾.
He is indeed able to bring man back after death.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And Mindal narrated to me from Layth from Mujāhid, who said: He is indeed able to return the fluid into the urethra.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلرَّجْعِ﴾.
It begins with rain, then returns with it every year.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدْعِ﴾.
It splits open with plants.
